locations.name: Sagrada Família
locations.short_description: Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece — the most visited monument in Spain.
locations.long_description: Construction began in 1882. Gaudí took over in 1883 and dedicated his life to it until his death in 1926. Anticipated completion: 2026.

locations.name: Park Güell
locations.short_description: Gaudí's hilltop park with sweeping views over Barcelona.
locations.long_description: Originally designed as a residential estate, Park Güell was donated to the city in 1922. The monumental zone requires a timed entry ticket.

regulatory_alert.message: Bicycles are not allowed inside the monumental zone. Please use the Bicipark racks at the entrance.

locations.name: Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)
locations.short_description: Medieval streets — dismount zone. Cycling prohibited. Fine: €500.
locations.long_description: The Barri Gòtic is a pedestrian-priority zone with extremely narrow medieval streets. Cycling is prohibited. You must dismount and walk your bike.

regulatory_alert.message: DISMOUNT ZONE — You have entered the Gothic Quarter. Cycling is prohibited here. Fine: €500. Please walk your bike.

locations.name: Camp Nou
locations.short_description: Home of FC Barcelona — the largest stadium in Europe.
locations.long_description: Camp Nou holds over 99,000 fans. The stadium experience tour lets you walk through the tunnel and sit in the directors' box.

quizzes.question: In what year did Gaudí die, leaving the Sagrada Família unfinished?
quizzes.explanation: Antoni Gaudí was struck by a tram on Gran Via in 1926. He died three days later aged 73.

quizzes.question: How many towers will the Sagrada Família have when fully complete?
quizzes.explanation: The final design includes 18 towers: 12 for the Apostles, 4 for the Evangelists, 1 for the Virgin Mary, and 1 central tower for Jesus Christ.

quizzes.question: Park Güell was originally designed to be a…
quizzes.explanation: Eusebi Güell commissioned Gaudí to design a garden city of 60 housing plots. Only two houses were ever built, and the project was abandoned in 1914.

faqs.question: Can I lock my bike at the Sagrada Família?
faqs.answer: Yes. There are Bicipark open racks on Avinguda de Gaudí (east side) and Carrer de Provença (north side). Do not lock to railings or barriers — wardens issue removal notices.

faqs.question: Do I need to book tickets in advance?
faqs.answer: Yes — strongly recommended. Same-day tickets are almost never available. Book via the official Sagrada Família website or GetYourGuide (link below) for skip-the-line access.

faqs.question: Can I bring my bicycle inside Park Güell?
faqs.answer: No. Bicycles are prohibited inside the ticketed monumental zone. Lock up at the designated Bicipark racks on Carrer d'Olot before the entrance gates.

faqs.question: Why can't I cycle through the Gothic Quarter?
faqs.answer: The Barri Gòtic is a pedestrian-priority zone. Barcelona's traffic ordinance prohibits cycling in these streets. The fine is €500. You must dismount and walk your bike.

faqs.question: Where can I park near the Gothic Quarter?
faqs.answer: Use the Bicibox station on Plaça de Catalunya (24/7, free, requires PIN from the Bicibox app) or the Bicipark racks near La Rambla entrance.

tours.name: Gaudí Highlights
tours.description: Sagrada Família, Casa Milà and Park Güell — Gaudí's three essentials in one ride.

details.infraction: Riding a bicycle on pedestrian pavement (sidewalk)
details.notes: Applies city-wide. Can be doubled in pedestrian priority zones.

details.infraction: Using headphones in both ears simultaneously while cycling
details.notes: One ear is permitted. Blocking both ears = €100 fine.
